Eli (sales): Quick—MedGrid wants a Private deploy POC. They asked: peering vs PrivateLink recommendation, how to whitelist one egress IP, minimal firewall ports, and whether SNI/original client IP survive. Need concise bullets for their SOC.

Rina (netops): Short bullets: Peering = preserves original source IP (good for netflow/audit). PrivateLink = connector traffic appears from ENI IPs in their VPC (so you won’t see client IP at network layer).

Hector (eng): For HTTP(S) over PrivateLink we can add X-Forwarded-For / X-Original-Client-IP headers. For raw TLS streams the source will be ENI; app-level header only for HTTP.

Lena (security): If SOC requires cryptographic linkage to client IP, peering is advised. If app-level audit is sufficient, PrivateLink + headers works. SNI is visible in ClientHello unless TLS interception / ESNI used.

Rina (netops): Minimal ports: outbound TCP 443 to our control plane CIDR (we'll supply exact CIDR); if PrivateLink allow inbound TCP 443 from connector ENI range; if peering allow 443 across the peering route.

Eli (sales): Single egress IP for their firewall?

Rina (netops): Yes—have them NAT connector egress through their NAT Gateway/EIP. With peering source IPs are preserved so they control NAT at edge. With PrivateLink ENI is internal but egress can be routed via NAT to a single EIP.

handshake-bot: Handshake created: https://redwood.internal/handshakes/MG-321 — netops to attach ENI CIDRs + SG snippet.

Eli (sales): Great—I'll paste these bullets into the SOC note. Rina, can you drop the sample SG + NAT pattern into the ticket by EOD?

Rina (netops): On it. Also note: if they expect >500Mbps sustained, recommend peering + TGW + dedicated connector subnet to avoid MTU fragmentation.

Hector (eng): And if they need burst RPS SLA, we should propose a Dedicated capacity commit (commercial).

Lena (security): Paste-ready SOC lines: "Data: request metadata and operational logs are retained per customer-configured retention; payloads are not stored unless explicitly enabled. Keys: customer-managed KMS/HSM supported."

Eli (sales): Thanks all — sending to MedGrid now. :thumbsup:
